subtype: Stage 1: A new claim on attention [Actor]
passage:
Daycare note, Tuesday pickup.
Chirag (5) was building with blocks when his mother, Lavanya, arrived carrying baby Lakshay with a shiny new rattle. Chirag ran to her, then saw the baby on her hip. He stopped. He grabbed the rattle and hit Lakshay's hand with it. Lakshay cried. Chirag's lip shook.
I knelt beside him. "You wanted Mumma's lap too." He nodded and pressed his face into my shoulder.
I suggested Lavanya give Chirag a hug first at pickup tomorrow. 🙂
— Charu Miss

qa.q: What was baby Lakshay holding?
qa.a: Lakshay was holding a shiny new rattle.

qa.q: What was Chirag feeling when he saw the baby on his mother's hip?
qa.a: He felt left out and hurt, even though he loves his mother and brother, and he could not say it in words.

qa.q: What small step did Charu Miss suggest?
qa.a: Charu Miss suggested Lavanya hug Chirag first at pickup, so he feels he still has his place.

qa.q: How might Lavanya feel seeing Chirag hit the baby?
qa.a: She may feel upset and confused, not realising at first that Chirag is feeling pushed aside.

grounding: It shows a five-year-old boy seeing his baby brother on his mother's lap with a shiny toy, feeling hurt and acting it out by grabbing and hitting.

passage: In Navsari, the afternoon was hot and still. Zubin, five, came in from the lane and saw his baby brother Kaizad on Mamma's lap. Ritu Masi had brought Kaizad a shiny spinning top. Zubin stood by the door. Then he marched over, grabbed the top and pushed Kaizad's arm. Kaizad wailed. "Zubin!" Mamma said. Zubin threw the top on the floor and ran behind the cupboard. Ritu Masi found him there, hugging his knees. She sat down beside him and opened her arms.

qa.q: What did Ritu Masi bring for Kaizad?
qa.a: She brought him a shiny spinning top.

qa.q: Why did Zubin grab the top and push Kaizad?
qa.a: He felt hurt and left out seeing Kaizad on Mamma's lap with a new toy, and he did not have words for it.

qa.q: How could Mamma help Zubin at this stage?
qa.a: She could make room for Zubin on her lap too and say, "You wanted a turn with me," so he feels seen instead of only scolded.

qa.q: How does Ritu Masi see Zubin hiding behind the cupboard?
qa.a: She sees a sad little boy who needs comfort, so she sits beside him and opens her arms.

grounding: It illustrates a five-year-old boy who sees his baby brother getting a parent's lap and a shiny toy, and shows his hurt by grabbing and pushing.

passage:
"Mumma, why is Chintu on your lap again?"

"Because he's sleepy, Lalit."

"I'm sleepy too."

"Come sit next to me, then."

"No. I want the lap."

"Lalit, there's no room right now."

"Chintu got a new rattle. A shiny one."

"You have lots of toys, baby."

"I want THAT one."

Lalit grabbed the rattle out of Chintu's hand. Chintu wailed.

"Lalit!"

Lalit threw the rattle on the floor and hid behind the sofa, arms crossed, lip wobbling.

Sunaina put Chintu down and knelt by the sofa. "Did you want a turn on my lap?"

A tiny nod.

qa.q: What did Chintu get that Lalit wanted?
qa.a: A new shiny rattle.

qa.q: Why did Lalit grab the rattle?
qa.a: He felt left out and hurt seeing Chintu on Mumma's lap with a new toy, and couldn't say it, so it came out as grabbing.

qa.q: What did Sunaina do that helped?
qa.a: She knelt by Lalit and named what he wanted, a turn on her lap, instead of only scolding him.

qa.q: How might Chintu feel when the rattle is snatched?
qa.a: He is probably startled and upset, which is why he wails.

grounding: Lalit sees his baby brother on Mumma's lap with a shiny toy and, unable to say he feels left out, grabs the toy, until his mother names what he wants.

subtype: Stage 1: A new claim on attention [Actor]
passage:
Preschool note, Thursday

Zubin (5) has been unsettled since his baby brother arrived. At pick-up today, his mother held the baby, who had a new soft giraffe. Zubin watched, then pulled the giraffe away and pushed the baby's foot. He looked confused and tearful afterwards.

Earlier he had made a card "for Mama and baby" with a big heart around both. He loves his brother and feels pushed aside, and cannot say it yet.

I showed his mother the card and suggested special time for Zubin each day.

— Elizabeth (class teacher)

qa.q: What did Zubin draw on his card?
qa.a: A big heart around Mama and the baby.

qa.q: Why might Zubin have pushed his brother's foot?
qa.a: He feels both love and hurt, pushed aside by the new baby, and can't say it in words, so it comes out as pulling and pushing.

qa.q: What did Elizabeth suggest, and why could it help?
qa.a: Special time just for Zubin each day, so he feels sure of his own place and doesn't need to grab attention.

qa.q: How might Zubin's mother feel seeing the card after the push?
qa.a: She may feel relieved and touched, seeing that Zubin also loves his brother.

grounding: A teacher's note shows five-year-old Zubin, loving but feeling pushed aside by his baby brother, expressing it by grabbing and pushing.

subtype: Stage 1: A new claim on attention [Actor]
passage:
In the anganwadi courtyard, Irfan's Ammi fed baby Imran on her lap. Sangeeta didi, the anganwadi worker, gave Imran a bright red rattle.

Irfan watched. He was five, and until two months ago, that lap had been his.

He walked over, snatched the rattle and ran to the neem tree. Imran cried.

"Irfan! Give it back!"

Sangeeta didi went and crouched beside him. "You wanted something new too?"

He nodded, hiccuping.

"And maybe a turn with Ammi?"

A bigger nod. Sangeeta didi took his hand and walked him back to his mother.

qa.q: What colour was the rattle?
qa.a: Bright red.

qa.q: What was Irfan feeling when he snatched the rattle?
qa.a: He felt hurt and left out, missing his place on Ammi's lap, and couldn't say it, so he snatched and ran.

qa.q: What did Sangeeta didi do that helped?
qa.a: She crouched beside Irfan and gently named what he wanted, something new and a turn with Ammi, instead of scolding.

qa.q: How might Ammi feel when Irfan comes back holding Sangeeta didi's hand?
qa.a: She might feel relieved and understand that Irfan needs time with her too.

grounding: Five-year-old Irfan sees his baby brother on Ammi's lap with a new rattle and, unable to say he feels left out, snatches it until an adult names his feeling.

passage: In the kitchen of their Cape Town flat, baby Emil sat on Mama's lap, shaking a shiny red rattle that jingled. Everyone smiled at him. Thabo, who was five, stood by the table holding his drawing of a lion. Nobody looked at it. He watched Emil for a long time. Then he walked over, grabbed the rattle and threw it on the floor. Emil wailed. Mama said, "Thabo!" Thabo's lip wobbled. A minute later he patted Emil's foot, very gently, and then hid behind the curtain.

qa.q: What was Thabo holding while he stood by the table?
qa.a: His drawing of a lion.

qa.q: Why did Thabo grab the rattle?
qa.a: He felt left out and hurt that nobody looked at his lion drawing, and since he could not say it, it came out as grabbing.

qa.q: What could Mama do next to help Thabo?
qa.a: After settling Emil, she could look at Thabo's lion and say something like, 'It's hard when the baby gets all the looks,' so his feeling has words.

qa.q: What is it like for Emil when the rattle is grabbed?
qa.a: Emil is startled and upset, wailing when his shiny toy is suddenly snatched and thrown.

grounding: Shows a five-year-old who loves and resents his baby brother, his hurt coming out as grabbing because he cannot put it into words.
